arStrings.szText: I misjudged you, barbarian. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw an ignorant savage, charging ahead on instinct alone.
I misjudged you, druid. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a dumb animal, pretending at wisdom yet killing without thought.
I misjudged you, necromancer. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a dabbling novice, playing at the tools of Death.
I misjudged you, paladin. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a self-righteous buffoon, raging against the inevitable.
I misjudged you, rogue. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a cutthroat with delusions of heroism.
I misjudged you, sorcerer. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a fool academic, meddling in matters beyond their intellect.
I misjudged you, spiritborn. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a backward primitive, fighting like an animal caught in a trap.
I misjudged you, warlock. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a demon-haunted vagabond, a hair's breadth away from corruption.
I misjudged you, wanderer. When I first laid eyes on you, I saw a brave idiot, fighting for survival alone.
I have only just learned how you've been misguided. Tyrael offers you false hope...the same he once offered to me, until he buried me alive.
Go to him. Ask him why I have no name.
